Information since May points to a tight labor market and moderate growth, but soft business fixed investment and sub-2% inflation. Within standard New Keynesian/Taylor-rule perspectives (e.g., Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), holding the funds rate while signaling readiness to ease reflects risk-management under rising uncertainty. Elevated policy uncertainty (Baker, Bloom, Davis) and financing constraints can depress capex, consistent with the observed softness in business investment. A flatter Phillips curve with anchored expectations helps explain muted inflation despite strong employment, while declining market-based inflation compensation aligns with term-structure evidence that long-rate inflation premia can fall (Ang and Piazzesi; Cochrane and Piazzesi). Operationally, reliance on IOR and ON RRP to maintain the target range is consistent with the modern floor system and Goodfriend’s policy implementation insights. Net tone: cautiously positive on activity, dovish on inflation and risks.
